seo_desc: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, Ujjain: Bhasma Aarti booking rules (one per mobile every 90 days), dress code, darshan timings, the legend and how to reach.
label: Mahakaleshwar, Ujjain
blurb: The south-facing Lord of Time, by the Shipra
sub: Shri Mahakaleshwar, the Jyotirlinga of Ujjain, is the only one of the twelve that faces south. The legend of Mahakal, the pre-dawn Bhasma Aarti and how to book it, the dress code, the phone rule, festival crowds and the easiest ways to reach.
q: Where is Mahakaleshwar temple and why is it sacred?
answer: Shri Mahakaleshwar temple stands in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, near the Shipra river, about 55 km from Indore. It is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas, where Shiva is worshipped as Mahakala, the lord of time — and the only one of the twelve that faces south. Its Bhasma Aarti begins at about 4 am and must be booked online.
facts: the only one of the 12 Jyotirlingas
intro: Ujjain — the ancient Avanti, or Avantika — is one of Hinduism's seven sacred cities, and Baba Mahakal is its guardian. Pilgrims usually bathe at Ram Ghat on the Shipra, walk through the Shri Mahakal Lok corridor and take darshan of the self-manifested (svayambhu) linga. Many also try to attend the Bhasma Aarti, the temple's famous pre-dawn ritual. The temple is open all year.

According to temple tradition, the shrine rises in three levels: Mahakaleshwar at the bottom, an Omkareshwar shrine in the middle, and Nagchandreshwar at the top, which opens for just one day a year on Nag Panchami. The middle-level shrine is not the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga, which stands on the Narmada about 140 km away.

story.lead: The Koti Rudra Samhita of the Shiva Purana tells how Shiva came to stay in Avanti as Mahakala. This is how tradition tells it.
beats: In Avanti lived a learned Brahmin, Vedapriya, whose four sons worshipped an earthen linga every single day.
Strengthened by a boon from Brahma, the demon Dushana came down from the Ratnamala hills and set about stopping all prayer in the city. The family kept chanting Shiva's name.
As the demon rushed at them, it is believed the earth beside their linga split open and Shiva rose in his fearsome Mahakala form — with a single roar, Dushana was reduced to ash.
The devotees begged him to stay and protect Avanti for ever. Tradition holds that he remained here as the self-born, south-facing Mahakaleshwar.
more: The same tradition tells of King Chandrasena and a young cowherd, Shrikhar, whose devotion protected Ujjain. South is the direction of death, and as Mahakala — lord of time and death — Shiva here faces south. These are stories of faith, told as tradition rather than history. Mahakaleshwar is third in the Shiva Purana's list of the twelve Jyotirlingas and in the Dwadasha Jyotirlinga stotram (उज्जयिन्यां महाकालम्).

extra_sections.label: Bhasma Aarti
extra_sections.h2: How to book the Mahakal Bhasma Aarti
extra_sections.html:
The Bhasma Aarti is performed before dawn, starting at about 4 am every day, when the jyotirlinga is anointed with sacred ash. In the past the ash was said to come from a cremation pyre; today it is prepared from cow dung, according to MP Tourism.

Entry needs a prior online booking on the temple's official website — MP Tourism advises booking about a month ahead. Since 22 June 2026 the temple committee allows one Bhasma Aarti permission per mobile number every 90 days, VIP protocol included. Arrive an hour or more before the time on your pass.

For worship in the sanctum, including the Bhasma Aarti, men wear a dhoti and women a saree. Booking procedures have changed several times in 2026, so check the rules on the official website before you travel — and ignore agents or look-alike sites selling "tatkal" or "VIP" passes.

extra_sections.label: History
extra_sections.h2: A short history of Mahakaleshwar temple
extra_sections.html:
In 1234–35 Sultan Iltutmish raided Ujjain and the temple complex was destroyed. It was rebuilt in the 18th century under Maratha (Scindia) rule by Diwan Ramachandra (Baba) Sukthankar.

On 11 October 2022 the Prime Minister dedicated Phase I of the Shri Mahakal Lok corridor, a wide landscaped approach to the temple.

cards: Devi Ahilyabai Holkar Airport, Indore, is about 55 km away by road.
Ujjain Junction is about 2 km from the temple.
Ujjain is about 55 km from Indore on the Indore–Ujjain highway; e-rickshaws and autos run to the temple from the station and bus stand.
The Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga on the Narmada is about 140 km away via Indore — most pilgrims pair the two.

items: Book only on the official site
Bhasma Aarti and quick-darshan bookings are made only on the temple's official website. Agent sites that rank for "bhasma aarti booking" are not the temple — never pay them.
Only one Bhasma Aarti permission is allowed per mobile number every 90 days — pick your date carefully and book well ahead.
Pack a dhoti (men) and saree (women) for the Bhasma Aarti and sanctum worship.
Mobiles and cameras are not allowed inside; use the lockers or leave them at your hotel.
The Bhasma Aarti means reporting in the small hours, and the Mahakal Lok walkways are long. Ask at the help desk about wheelchair help, and consider an ordinary daytime darshan instead.
Harsiddhi Mata temple (counted as a Shakti Peeth in many traditions) about 0.5 km, Ram Ghat on the Shipra about 1 km, Kal Bhairav and Sandipani Ashram about 5 km each.

itinerary.h2: A two-day Ujjain and Omkareshwar yatra
days: Reach Indore or Ujjain and check in. Darshan at Mahakaleshwar and a walk through Mahakal Lok, then Harsiddhi Mata and the evening aarti at Ram Ghat. Next morning: the Bhasma Aarti if you have a booking, then Kal Bhairav and Sandipani Ashram.
Drive about 140 km to Omkareshwar for darshan of the fourth Jyotirlinga and Mamleshwar, then return to Indore for your onward journey.

faqs: What time is the Mahakal Bhasma Aarti?
It begins at about 4 am every day, according to MP Tourism. Devotees are asked to arrive an hour or more early — follow the reporting time printed on your pass.
How do I book the Bhasma Aarti at Mahakaleshwar?
Only online, on the temple's official website — MP Tourism advises about a month ahead. Since 22 June 2026 the temple allows one Bhasma Aarti permission per mobile number every 90 days.
What is the dress code for the Bhasma Aarti?
For worship in the sanctum, including the Bhasma Aarti, men wear a dhoti and women a saree. Modest clothing is expected for general darshan.
Is the Bhasma Aarti ash from cremation pyres?
Not today. MP Tourism says the ash used in the Bhasma Aarti is now prepared from cow dung, although tradition speaks of ash from a cremation pyre.
The temple opens for the Bhasma Aarti at about 4 am and stays open until late night. Exact hours are not published on an official source we could verify, so confirm locally.
South is the direction of death. As Mahakala, lord of time and death, Shiva here faces south — the only south-facing temple among the 12 Jyotirlingas.
Are mobile phones allowed inside Mahakaleshwar temple?
No. Mobiles and cameras are not allowed inside; lockers are available.
How far is Omkareshwar from Ujjain?
About 140 km by road via Indore, according to the Shri Omkareshwar Mandir Trust. Many pilgrims visit both Jyotirlingas in two days.
